transcript:
This message comes from Mattress Firm.
Restless partner keeping you up?
Mattress Firm sleep experts can match you with a Tempur-Pedic that absorbs motion.
Save up to $1,000 on select Tempur-Pedic split-king sleep systems during the Black Friday sale.
They make sleep easy.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
The CIA has been hacked the latest in a series of computer problems in government organizations and high-profile private companies.
NPR's Greg Myry has details.
The intrusion into the CIA computer network took place in an unclassified part of the system.
This is according to a person with knowledge of the breach who is not authorized to speak publicly.
That source says no classified parts of the computer network were affected.
Several leading companies, including Microsoft, Apple, and major banks, have suffered computer failures this month.
So has the National Security Agency.
However, those outages were attributed to internal efforts to patch or upgrade software flaws that have been detected by AI programs.
The CIA hack was carried out by a cyber intruder who has not been identified.
Greg Myry, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump has awarded former New York City mayor and political ally Rudy Giuliani with the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
Trump honored Giuliani with the country's highest civilian award and a private ceremony at the White House.
No press allowed, as NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
President Trump has repeatedly referred to Rudy Giuliani as the greatest mayor in the history of New York City.
The White House hailed his "lasting impact" on both New York City and the nation.
Giuliani is famous for his role leading New York in the aftermath of the September 11, 2001 attacks.
He ran unsuccessfully for president in 2008, but then had quite a fall in the public eye.
Giuliani, who served as Trump's personal lawyer during his efforts to overturn the 2020 election, was later sanctioned by the courts and was disbarred in both New York and Washington for making false statements about the election.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News, The White House.
With the holiday shopping season about to kick off, Best Buy says sales are way up. The company says consumers are shopping for computers, laptops and things like A.I. glasses, as NPR's Alina Seljuk reports.
Best Buy's report blew all forecasts out of the water.
The company says in the latest quarter, its sales in the U.S. grew 6.2 percent.
One reason was higher prices driven by the rise in the cost of memory chips.
But people also shopped a lot. Executives called out laptops and desktops, presumably for back to school and college.
Best Buy also sells lots of trading cards that are in huge demand, also gaming gear and mobile phones.
All this was before the new release of the blockbuster video game Grand Theft Auto, which is one of the reasons Best Buy is also dramatically raising its future financial forecast.
The retailer is additionally one of the first big box stores to recently launch on TikTok shop. Alina Seljuk, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
U.S. Army appears to be on track toward the detonation of a five-ton stockpile of degraded bomb-making material at a facility in southeast Iowa.
The stockpile is said to be detonated Wednesday morning to prevent what the Army says could be a dangerous, spontaneous explosion.
The plan has sparked public concern, though, about possible health and environmental impacts the Army says is taking numerous precautions and an area stretching five miles southwest of the site has been recommended for evacuation.
The rate of newborns receiving vaccination against hepatitis B has fallen sharply from 80 percent in 2022 to just under 66 percent this year.
That's according to new findings in the New England Journal of Medicine.
Here's NPR's Maria Godoy.
Last winter, a federal advisory panel to the CDC voted to end a longstanding recommendation that all newborns get the hepatitis B vaccine.
The new study offers the first glimpse of how vaccination rates have changed since then.
Study co-author Nina Masters of health care data analytics firm Triveda says while vaccination rates had been sliding for several years before the panels vote.
There's been a lot of national level miscommunication and confusing information, changing recommendations, and it's certainly not helping parents to feel clear on what they should do.
Hepatitis B infections in infants are highly likely to lead to chronic infection and serious complications like liver cancer later in life. Maria Godoy, NPR News.
Stocks are retreating in Asia amid losses in the tech sector. I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.
